narrative.title: Re-cabling the Server Hall
narrative.scenario: A server hall's racks are linked by cables, some of them redundant. Technicians may unplug a cable between two already-linked racks and re-run it between any disconnected pair. The facilities lead needs the fewest such re-cabling moves to make the whole hall one network — or proof that there simply aren't enough cables to go round.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n (racks 0..n-1) and a list connections where [a, b] is a link between racks a and b.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the minimum number of cable moves needed to connect all racks, or -1 if impossible.

testCases.explanation: Racks 0-1-2 form one cluster and rack 3 is isolated; the loop's spare cable reaches it.
The hub already links every rack.

hintLevels: Level 1: Each isolated cluster needs exactly one incoming cable, and one cable can serve one cluster.
Level 2: Count components with union-find; the answer is components minus one.
Level 3: Feasibility first — fewer than n-1 cables can never connect n racks, whatever the shape.
